page: Amazon Web Services m8in.48xlarge is an eighth-generation, network-optimized general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with dedicated x86_64 Intel processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system provides 192 virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory. This architecture adheres to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, allocating 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

A primary architectural characteristic of this instance type is its network and interconnect throughput. With a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps, the instance accommodates extreme data transfer requirements. The instance features no local NVMe storage and includes no integrated GPUs, requiring all persistent storage and operational volumes to run over network-attached Elastic Block Store or remote storage tiers.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance aggregates massive compute and memory density into a single host footprint, delivering high throughput consolidation for large workloads. The absence of bundled ephemeral disks reduces local storage maintenance overhead, though operations heavily dependent on high-speed scratch disks will incur network transit over the storage fabric.

The m8in.48xlarge is targeted at large-scale enterprise applications that demand substantial memory bandwidth and network interconnects. Fitting deployments include high-throughput distributed databases, large in-memory caching nodes, large enterprise resource planning systems, big data analytics clusters, and intensive containerized microservices fleets.
